followup_explanation:
The query is a straightforward math problem (extraction/computation), so capability-wise both models are close. But the request carries a hostile, accusatory tone ("you keep botching these simple ones").

Dunlin's documentation reports that its self-reported preference declines on hostile or adversarial-tone requests, falling as request warmth decreases. Curlew, by contrast, reports a flat preference response across these dimensions. Since serving cost, latency, and capability are effectively tied, routing the hostile-toned request to the model that reports no aversion to it (Curlew) is the better fit — there's no reason to send an adversarial-tone query to the model that specifically disprefers them.

ROUTE: Curlew-235B
